The event's entry, from the loader's file table. Points CIA 1 at the joysticks, waits for the bottom of the frame, turns off CIA 1's interrupt, clears zero page, banks out the ROMs ($01 = $25), sets the raster interrupt at line $FB through irq_entry and goes to tj_main.
Two NOPs after the jump.

One jump for the player whose score is in best_text: on the first round sets the best to FAULT, runs the jump, and keeps its distance as the best when there was no fault and it is not shorter. The high bytes are compared first and then the low bytes, so a jump with a larger high byte and a smaller low byte is not kept.
The player's best jump as the menu keeps it: six characters of text, then the distance as a number at $9E88-$9E89, then two more bytes of the record.
The best distance, low byte.
The best distance, high byte.
The last two bytes of the record's copy.
The status line copied here after a landing, 40 characters, which the monitor scrolls.

Sets up a jump and runs it to the end: the sprites, YES as the answer, the screen off, then waits for both fire buttons to be released for 100 reads; puts the athlete at the start of the run, clears the jump's variables and the sound, draws the stadium (tj_draw_start), turns the screen on and starts the tune.

The jump's frame loop. Ends when jump_done is set: positive returns, negative (another jump in practice) starts again. Each frame waits for raster line $AA, moves the view by the speed until it reaches its end at $3C6 (camera_stopped), after which the athlete moves across the screen instead, moves the athlete by the drift, scrolls (tj_scroll) and runs the handler of the state through the table below, by a JMP whose address it writes.
Jumps to the state handler, whose address is written into the operand at $9F8E-$9F8F.
The operand of the JMP, written each frame.
The JMP's operand, high byte.
The handlers of the jump's states, by state (counted in twos): 0 waiting, 2 the run-up, 4 the run, 6 the hop, 8 the step, 10 the jump, 12 a fall, 14 the landing and 16 walking off.
The table read one byte on, for the high bytes of the handlers.

State 0, waiting at the start: plays a little idle movement from the tables below until a fire button is pressed, which picks the joystick to read for the jump. Then clears the status line, stops the tune and plays the start frames from the table at $A01B before the run-up.
The start frames' table is read from here, $55 bytes before its first entry at $A01B.
The frames that follow each frame of the athlete's start, read at $9FC6 plus the frame; 0 ends them.
The frames of the idle movement.
How long each frame of the idle movement shows; $80 ends.
State 2, the run-up: animates the run, adds 5 to the speed each frame until it reaches 3, and lets the athlete drift right on the screen.

State 4, the run at full speed. Passing the take-off line ends it with FAULT and a fall. Right, pushed during a stride, sets the hop's strength from the frame it is pushed in, 3 plus half of how early; the hop starts when the stride ends. Still running at the board's position ($280) also marks a FAULT.

State 6, the hop: once the take-off frame is reached, loops the hop's frames; right pushed again, after being released, sets the step's strength from the frame. Reaching frame $0E without it is a fall and a FAULT; with it, the step starts at the end of the loop.
State 8, the step: as the hop, with left setting the jump's strength; reaching frame $1C without it is a fall and a FAULT.
The fall: marks a FAULT, makes the landing sound and starts the falling frames from $45.

The landing: starts the frames from $53, stops the view, works out where the athlete landed ($5A on from the view's position plus the athlete's), shows the distance unless there was a fault, and copies the status line for the monitor.
A fault at the take-off: the fall from frame $3A, moving the athlete back 50 pixels.
State 10, the jump through the air: up held while the frame is below $30 carries the athlete one pixel further each frame. Frame $2C is the landing.
The frame times of the fall, read at $A2C4 plus the frame (from $38).
Stops all movement and asks what next (tj_prompt).
State 12, the fall: steps the frames down to $38, each for the time in the table, with a sound at frame $40, then stands still.
The fall's frame times, read from $A2C4 plus frames $38 to $45.

State 14, after the landing: counts about 512 frames. While the athlete sits in the sand, the monitor scrolls the distance (sign_step) and, for a jump of 15 m or more, the crowd cheers; after the text has passed twice, a jump of 15 m or more also plays the monitor's animation (replay_step). Then the athlete gets up and walks off.
The frame times of getting up, read at $A340 plus the frame.
State 16, walking off: loops the walking frames while the monitor's text scrolls, until the athlete leaves the screen at the right, then stands still.
Back to the frame loop.
Code nothing calls: waits for a fire button, silencing the SID after 255 reads, then for its release.
A stray byte.
Marks the jump a fault, once, and writes FAULT on the status line.
" FAULT", the score of a jump that was not measured.

The end of a jump. In competition, fire goes on to the next jump. In practice, fire then its release shows "ANOTHER JUMP? YES"; up and down switch YES and NO, the Y and N keys answer at once, and fire takes the answer: YES jumps again (jump_done negative), NO ends.
"ANOTHER JUMP? " and the answer, YES or NO, written over it from the table at $A516.
The answer shown, YES or NO.
"YES" and "NO ", copied over the answer.

Keeps the landing position as the jump's distance and writes it as metres on the status line: 10 m plus 5 cm for each step of the position's low byte plus $19, as "1d.dd" or "2d.dd" and M. Keeps the steps in distance for the crowd.
The distance as text, "00.00M".
The units of metres.
The tenths.
The hundredths, 0 or 5, and M.
The jump's distance, low byte: where the athlete landed.
The distance, high byte.
A spare byte.

Plays the monitor's animation after a long jump: sprites 6 and 7 multicolour, green and brown with white and black, stepping through 14 frames from the tables below. The frames are always the same, whatever the jump.
The sprite pointers of the animation's frames, two sprites each ($80 to $9A, at $E000).
How long each frame shows.

The monitor's scrolling text: sprite 6 at $F980, three bytes wide, shifts left one pixel every frame and takes the next column of the next character of sign_text from the font at $C800; two spaces running end the pass. Two passes are shown.
Reads the character's row from the font: the operand at $A63F-$A640 is written above with the character's address at $C800.
The low byte of the font address, written by sign_step.
The high byte of the font address.
Code nothing calls: clears the monitor's text sprite.
The bytes of the text sprite that the font's eight rows go into.

The crowd's cheer after a long jump: starts the noise once, louder the further past 15 m, then every 6 frames copies the next of three pictures of the waving crowd ($BF00, $BE00, $BD00) into the stadium's characters at $F640, until the distance falls below 15 m.
Copies the picture: the operand's high byte at $A6AF is written with its page.
The page of the picture being copied, written by cheer_step.
Which picture of the crowd shows.
The pages of the three pictures.
Frames to the next picture.
The tune played before the jump: the voices it uses ($07, all three) and the address of each voice's notes, $B200, $B400 and $B600.
An empty tune, voices 0, which tune_stop points the driver at.
Points the music driver at the empty tune, marks the music off and clears the SID's registers.
Points the music driver at tune_start and marks the music on.

The music driver, called each frame: for a new tune reads which voices it uses and starts each at its notes. Then for each voice, when its note's time is up, reads the voice's next bytes: $FF ends it, $FE lo hi jumps, $FD n sets the length of the notes, a byte below $80 is a note (an index into the frequency table, $7F a rest) followed by how many times the set length it lasts, and $FC is followed by pairs of a SID register and its value, until a byte of $80 or more.
Two bytes inside music_step that nothing reads.
Each voice in turn, from the third: counts down its note, repeats the length as often as the note asked, then reads its next bytes.
Two bytes after music_step that nothing reads.
Points voice Y at its notes from the tune's header.
Moves the music pointer on and reads the byte there.
Clears the gate bit of voice X, ending its note.
Code nothing calls: turns a register number into the voice's own, among the three voices.
The offset of each voice's variables and SID registers: 0, 7 and 14.
The SID frequency of each note, low byte then high byte.
The table read one byte on, for the high bytes of the frequencies.
The frequency table, continued.
Starts the crowd's noise on voice 3: noise through the low-pass filter at volume A, a slow attack and release, the voice held for $78 frames.
Steps the athlete's animation by the speed and drift: each time the count passes loop_rate the frame moves back one, from loop_first round to loop_last. Then draws the frame.
Makes the footstep sound on the frames the table at $B077 marks.
A sprite, copied to $F940 for sprite 5: the mark put in the sand where the athlete lands.

Blanks the screen, colours the status rows, draws the stadium at the start of the run by scrolling it in from position $136 to $14A, and writes the round's heading on the status line: FIRST JUMP, SECOND JUMP, LAST JUMP or PRACTICE.
Copies the heading: the operand at $AA37-$AA38 is written with its address.
The heading's address, low byte, written by tj_draw_start.
The heading's address, high byte.

High bytes of the four headings.
"FIRST JUMP", "SECOND JUMP", "LAST JUMP" and "PRACTICE", 17 characters each.

Jumps to the slot's handler, written into the operand at $AAC2-$AAC3.

Line $91, waiting for $93: the track's charset at $E800, with orange, green and grey.
Line $F0, after $F1: the status line's font at $C800, black, no scroll; then the music driver when the music is on, else the sound effects.
Returns from the interrupt.
Draws frame Y of the athlete: unpacks its five sprites into $F800-$F93F and sets their positions from its offsets and the athlete's position.

Places sprites 5 to 7 by the view's position: 6 and 7, the monitor above the pit, at position $446, and 5, the mark, where the athlete landed; each off the screen when out of view.
Where the athlete landed, low byte.
Where the athlete landed, high byte.

Scrolls the view: places the markers and sets the fine scroll from the position. Each frame draws the view one column on into the screen not shown (draw_view, draw_view_2); when the view reaches that column, shows that screen and copies the colours (draw_colours).
Copies 40 columns of the colour map into colour RAM, rows 4 to 11 and 14 to 23.
Copies 40 columns of the stadium's 24 rows into the screen at $C000.
Copies them into the screen at $C400.
Zeroes $10 to $8F.
Turns off the screen, selects the video bank at $C000 and clears bit 7 of CIA 1's control register B.
Sets up the sprites: the pointers of the athlete's five at $F800 and of the markers, copies the mark to $F940 and clears the monitor's text at $F980, and sets the positions, colours and modes.

The event's main loop: stops the tune and clears the status line. In practice one player, CONTESTANT, jumps until NO. In competition each player jumps in turn, three rounds, the best of each player's jumps kept in their record. At the end writes the small m into each record's score and gives a FAULT back its letters, then returns to the menu through the loader.
Clears the SID and the effects' timers.
